title: Mike Vrabel Praises Former Titan Cairo Santos After Thursday Night Loss – NBC Sports Report
body:
The Tennessee Titans’ former head coach Mike Vrabel publicly praised the talent of former kicker Cairo Santos after the Brazilian veteran led the Buffalo Bills to a 24‑17 victory over the Titans on Thursday night, a game that ended with Santos converting a 44‑yard field goal in the final seconds to seal the win. The commendation comes despite the fact that Santos was cut by Tennessee just days after a disastrous Week 5 performance in which he missed four field‑goal attempts against the Bills, a night that proved to be a turning point for both men’s careers.

Vrabel, who has guided Tennessee to multiple playoff appearances since taking the helm in 2018, recalled the 2019 season when Santos was a reliable specialist for the Titans. “Cairo was a great teammate and a solid kicker for us,” Vrabel said in a post‑game interview. “He worked hard, and I’ve always respected his dedication to the game. Tonight he showed why he’s still a quality NFL player.” The former coach’s remarks underscore a rare moment of sportsmanship, as many coaches typically distance themselves from players they have recently released.

The Thursday night showdown was a stark contrast to the Titans’ earlier encounter with the Bills in Week 5, where Santos’ four missed field goals—two from inside 30 yards—contributed to a 20‑14 loss for Buffalo and a 21‑17 defeat for Tennessee. The poor showing prompted the Titans to release Santos the following day, a move that sparked debate among analysts about the fairness of dismissing a veteran after a single rough outing. Critics argued that the decision reflected the NFL’s unforgiving nature toward specialists, while supporters claimed that consistency is non‑negotiable for a team fighting for playoff positioning.

Santos, who entered the league as an undrafted free agent in 2014 and has since become one of the most accurate kickers in the league’s history, seized the opportunity with Buffalo to rewrite the narrative. After signing a one‑year contract with the Bills in March, he quickly earned the trust of head coach Sean McDermott. His decisive field goal on the final drive—after a 12‑play, 70‑yard march down the field—demonstrated poise under pressure, a trait that had once made him a favorite in Tennessee’s special‑teams unit. The kick not only gave Buffalo a three‑point edge but also marked Santos’ first game‑winning field goal since 2021, reigniting discussions about his potential longevity in the league.

The Titans, meanwhile, continue to grapple with special‑teams instability. Following Santos’ release, Tennessee experimented with several kickers throughout the season, none of whom have matched the reliability the team once enjoyed. The lack of a consistent long‑range option has forced the Titans to rely more heavily on offensive production, a strategy that may prove unsustainable against elite defenses. Vrabel’s acknowledgment of Santos’ skill set may hint at a broader reassessment of the organization’s approach to special teams, possibly prompting a renewed focus on scouting and development in that phase of the game.

Looking ahead, both men appear poised for redemption. Vrabel’s Titans are scheduled to face the Indianapolis Colts in Week 11, a divisional matchup that could serve as a litmus test for the team’s resilience after a string of close losses. For Santos, the spotlight will remain on Buffalo as they chase a playoff berth, and his performance will be closely monitored to see if he can sustain the confidence he displayed against his former club. The mutual respect expressed on Thursday underscores a fundamental truth in the NFL: talent endures, and even a single misstep does not erase a player’s legacy. As the season progresses, the narratives of both coach and kicker will continue to intersect, offering a compelling subplot to the broader drama of the 2024 campaign.
